points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 奥古斯都出生于罗马，原名盖乌斯·屋大维。他是尤利乌斯·凯撒的甥孙和养子。在凯撒被刺杀前，屋大维被指定为凯撒的继承人。尽管年轻且缺乏政治经验，屋大维迅速进入罗马政坛，与马克·安东尼和莱皮杜斯组成后三头同盟，共同追杀刺杀凯撒的元老院成员。这一时期，屋大维展现出非凡的政治智慧和军事才能，为日后掌权奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Augustus was born in Rome as Gaius Octavius Thurinus. He was the grandnephew and adopted son of Julius Caesar. Before Caesar's assassination, Octavius was named as Caesar's heir. Despite his youth and lack of political experience, Octavius quickly entered Roman politics, forming the Second Triumvirate with Mark Antony and Lepidus to hunt down the senators who assassinated Caesar. During this period, Octavius demonstrated extraordinary political wisdom and military talent, laying the foundation for his future rule.

points.title: 权力争夺
points.description: 凯撒死后，屋大维与安东尼和莱皮杜斯组成后三头同盟，共同统治罗马。然而，权力很快导致三人之间的冲突。屋大维首先击败了莱皮杜斯，随后与安东尼展开权力斗争。这一时期，屋大维巧妙地利用宣传和公共关系，将自己塑造为凯撒事业的合法继承者，同时发展自己的军事力量。最终，在亚克兴战役(公元前31年)中，屋大维彻底击败了安东尼和埃及女王克利奥帕特拉七世，成为罗马的唯一统治者。
points.descriptionEn: After Caesar's death, Octavius formed the Second Triumvirate with Antony and Lepidus to rule Rome. However, power soon led to conflict among the three. Octavius first defeated Lepidus, then engaged in a power struggle with Antony. During this period, Octavius skillfully used propaganda and public relations to portray himself as the legitimate heir to Caesar's cause while developing his own military forces. Finally, at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, Octavius decisively defeated Antony and Cleopatra VII, becoming the sole ruler of Rome.

points.title: 权力转型
points.description: 在击败安东尼后，屋大维面临如何在不引发内战的情况下巩固权力的挑战。他采取了一系列政治策略，逐步将权力集中在自己手中，同时表面上恢复共和制。公元前27年，屋大维向元老院'交还'权力，元老院则授予他'奥古斯都'的称号，意为'神圣的'或'至高无上的'。这一时期，奥古斯都巧妙地平衡了共和传统与个人权力，建立了元首制，为罗马带来了长期的稳定。
points.descriptionEn: After defeating Antony, Octavius faced the challenge of consolidating power without triggering civil war. He implemented a series of political strategies to gradually concentrate power in his own hands while ostensibly restoring the Republic. In 27 BC, Octavius 'returned' power to the Senate, which in turn granted him the title 'Augustus,' meaning 'revered' or 'majestic.' During this period, Augustus skillfully balanced republican traditions with personal power, establishing the Principate, bringing long-term stability to Rome.

points.title: 帝国建设
points.description: 作为罗马的第一位皇帝，奥古斯都进行了大规模的帝国建设。他改革了罗马的行政体系，建立了高效的官僚机构，重组了军队，并扩大了罗马的疆域。奥古斯都还大力推动公共工程建设，包括修复和建造神庙、公共浴场、引水道和道路等。在文化方面，他鼓励文学艺术发展，赞助维吉尔、贺拉斯等著名作家。奥古斯都统治时期被称为'罗马和平'(Pax Romana)，为罗马带来了近200年的和平与繁荣，奠定了罗马帝国的基础。
points.descriptionEn: As Rome's first emperor, Augustus undertook massive empire-building projects. He reformed Rome's administrative system, established an efficient bureaucracy, reorganized the military, and expanded Rome's territories. Augustus also promoted public construction, including repairing and building temples, public baths, aqueducts, and roads. Culturally, he encouraged literary and artistic development, sponsoring famous writers like Virgil and Horace. Augustus' reign is known as the 'Pax Romana,' bringing nearly 200 years of peace and prosperity to Rome and laying the foundation for the Roman Empire.

points.title: 军事扩张
points.description: 奥古斯都统治期间，罗马帝国进行了大规模的军事扩张。他完成了对西班牙、阿尔卑斯山地区和多瑙河流域的征服，将罗马的疆域扩展到莱茵河-多瑙河一线。奥古斯都还建立了罗马的边防体系，包括边境要塞和道路网络，以防御外族入侵。在东方，他通过外交手段控制了亚美尼亚和帕提亚等地区。奥古斯都的军事政策不仅扩大了罗马的领土，也为罗马带来了丰富的资源和奴隶，促进了罗马经济的繁荣。
points.descriptionEn: During Augustus' reign, the Roman Empire underwent massive military expansion. He completed the conquest of Spain, the Alpine regions, and the Danube basin, extending Rome's territory to the Rhine-Danube line. Augustus also established Rome's frontier defense system, including border forts and road networks, to defend against foreign invasions. In the East, he controlled regions like Armenia and Parthia through diplomatic means. Augustus' military policy not only expanded Rome's territory but also brought rich resources and slaves to Rome, promoting economic prosperity.

points.title: 社会改革
points.description: 奥古斯都还进行了一系列社会和道德改革，旨在恢复传统的罗马价值观。他颁布了《婚姻法》，鼓励婚姻和生育，限制奢侈行为。奥古斯还重建了许多古老的宗教仪式，并担任大祭司，强化了罗马的宗教传统。在法律方面，他编纂了《朱利安法典》，简化了法律程序，使法律更加公正。此外，奥古斯都还建立了消防队和警察系统，改善了城市管理和公共安全。这些改革措施不仅改变了罗马社会，也为后来的帝国治理提供了模式。
points.descriptionEn: Augustus also implemented a series of social and moral reforms aimed at restoring traditional Roman values. He enacted the 'Julian Laws' to encourage marriage and childbirth while restricting luxury. Augustus restored many ancient religious ceremonies and served as Pontifex Maximus, strengthening Roman religious traditions. Legally, he compiled the 'Julian Code,' simplifying legal procedures and making justice more accessible. Additionally, Augustus established fire brigades and police systems, improving urban management and public safety. These reforms not only transformed Roman society but also provided models for later imperial governance.

appraisal.zh: 奥古斯都被视为罗马从共和走向帝国的关键人物，他终结内战、开创“罗马和平”，以行政与军事改革奠定帝国两个世纪的繁荣，并巧妙平衡共和传统与个人权力。另一种看法认为，这套制度实为独裁的开端，以共和外衣掩盖权力集中，伴随清洗与对自由的限制，其王朝安排也为后来暴君的出现埋下伏笔。
appraisal.en: Augustus is seen as the pivotal figure in Rome's passage from Republic to Empire: he ended the civil wars, inaugurated the Pax Romana, and through administrative and military reform laid the basis for two centuries of prosperity, skillfully balancing Republican tradition with personal power. Another view holds that this system was dictatorship in Republican dress, masking concentrated power amid purges and restrictions on freedom, and that his dynastic arrangement paved the way for later tyrants.

supporter.zh: 奥古斯都被视为罗马最伟大的统治者之一，他结束了长期的共和制内战，建立了罗马帝国，带来了长达两个世纪的和平与繁荣。他的统治时期被称为'罗马和平'，为罗马文化、艺术和建筑的发展奠定了基础。奥古斯都的行政改革、军事扩张和基础设施建设使罗马成为地中海世界的中心，影响了西方文明的发展轨迹。他巧妙地平衡了共和传统与君主制，创造了一种新的政治制度，为罗马帝国带来了稳定和繁荣。
supporter.en: Augustus is regarded as one of Rome's greatest rulers, ending the long period of Republican civil wars and establishing the Roman Empire, bringing two centuries of peace and prosperity. His reign, known as the 'Pax Romana,' laid the foundation for the development of Roman culture, art, and architecture. Augustus' administrative reforms, military expansions, and infrastructure development made Rome the center of the Mediterranean world, influencing the trajectory of Western civilization. He skillfully balanced Republican traditions with monarchy, creating a new political system that brought stability and prosperity to the Roman Empire.

critic.zh: 批评者认为奥古斯都的统治实际上是独裁的开始，他通过表面上的共和制掩饰了个人权力的集中。他的统治时期也伴随着暴力和镇压，包括对政敌的清洗和对自由的限制。奥古斯都的道德改革被视为对个人自由的干涉，而他的军事扩张虽然带来了领土扩张，但也导致了大量战争和死亡。此外，奥古斯都建立的王朝制度为后来的暴君如尼禄和卡利古拉铺平了道路，最终导致了罗马帝国的衰落。
critic.en: Critics argue that Augustus' rule was essentially the beginning of dictatorship, masking the concentration of personal power under the facade of the Republic. His reign was also marked by violence and suppression, including the elimination of political opponents and restrictions on freedom. Augustus' moral reforms are seen as interference with personal liberties, and his military expansions, while expanding territory, also led to numerous wars and deaths. Furthermore, the dynastic system he established paved the way for later tyrants like Nero and Caligula, eventually contributing to the decline of the Roman Empire.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，奥古斯都被视为罗马从共和制向帝国制过渡的关键人物。他既是一位精明的政治家，也是一位独裁者；既带来了和平与繁荣，也限制了公民自由。奥古斯都的形象在历史文献中经过多次重塑，从古代史学家如塔西佗的批判，到现代学者的客观分析。在流行文化中，奥古斯都经常出现在文学、电影和艺术作品中，成为权力与政治智慧的象征。他的统治代表了罗马文明的巅峰，也预示了帝国后期的挑战与危机。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Augustus is viewed as a pivotal figure in Rome's transition from Republic to Empire. He was both a shrewd politician and a dictator; bringing peace and prosperity while limiting civil liberties. Augustus' image has been reshaped multiple times in historical sources, from the critiques of ancient historians like Tacitus to the objective analyses of modern scholars. In popular culture, Augustus frequently appears in literature, films, and art as a symbol of power and political wisdom. His reign represents the pinnacle of Roman civilization while also foreshadowing the challenges and crises of the later Empire.

self.zh: 我 found Rome a city of bricks and left it a city of marble。
self.en: I found Rome a city of bricks and left it a city of marble.
